intended_object: For a true proposition p, the canonical equivalence between the type of proofs of p and the one-element type PUnit (inferred from the docstring and name).
explanation: The body is `equivPUnit` (the equivalence between any type with a Unique instance and PUnit) applied to `uniqueProp h`. That instance says p has exactly one element, which holds by proof irrelevance since h proves p. So it is exactly the canonical equivalence between a true proposition and the one-element type. The statement is about propositions by nature, so there is no broader generality to ask for; its general form for any type with exactly one element is `equivPUnit`, which this definition specialises.
